task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.description: Review the reported collision account and supplied vehicle, party, insurance, damage-photo, and police-report information to identify the facts available for triage.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one ordinary two-car collision intake with the described materials available; reviewing them together takes about 9 minutes. This gathers the case facts once for use in later checks.

operational_subtasks.description: Compare the identified policyholder, vehicle, loss date, and reported circumstances with the policy and accessible claim or policy records; note apparent coverage concerns without making a final coverage decision.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one routine policy and record lookup taking about 7 minutes, using the facts already gathered rather than re-reviewing the intake. A complicated coverage question may need specialist attention, but final coverage determination is outside this task.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Assess claim information completeness and consistency
operational_subtasks.description: Determine whether the available information is sufficient for adjuster handling, identify missing documents or details, and compare the reported accounts and materials for material conflicts.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one routine completeness and consistency assessment taking about 6 minutes, relying on the materials already reviewed. A repair estimate is not presumed necessary at triage; this activity identifies gaps or conflicts but does not contact parties to resolve them.

operational_subtasks.description: Evaluate the gathered findings for reported injuries, conflicting accounts, indicators of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions, and determine whether routine or specialist handling is appropriate.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Screen each claim once against the stated escalation criteria; the incremental check is estimated at about 3 minutes because it uses the policy and information findings already available. This is a triage decision, not a fraud investigation or final liability or coverage decision.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Record triage findings and route the claim
operational_subtasks.description: Enter or communicate the relevant claim facts, information gaps, conflicts, possible coverage concerns, and handling recommendation to the appropriate routine or specialist claims team.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one concise handoff using findings already developed, taking about 4 minutes for entry or routing and communication. No separate narrative investigation or duplicate review is included.
